earth_site: Devil's Throat, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
environment_type: Lava tube / pit and subsurface shelter
lunar_analogue_target: Mare Tranquillitatis pit; lunar lava-tube and pit environments
evidence_from_team_checklist: The checklist says the UCLA team behind the lunar pit thermal study visited Devil's Throat and notes a size comparison in secondary coverage.
potential_exploration_use: Useful for cave/pit access concepts, subsurface mapping, thermal-environment instrumentation and robotic traverse planning.
analogy_limits: Earth gravity, atmosphere, weather, water and biological activity differ strongly; Earth tubes are much smaller than lunar candidates.
qualitative_match_assessment: High for lava-tube/pit process relevance; site-specific quantitative match not yet measured.
next_data_or_validation_step: Candidate; obtain georeferenced cave survey, LiDAR/point cloud, temperature and entrance geometry; verify permissions and access.

environment_type: Basaltic lava plains and lava tubes
evidence_from_team_checklist: Hawaii is listed as an Earth lead for basaltic lava plains and as a region with studied lava tubes.
potential_exploration_use: Basaltic surface materials and volcanic emplacement processes; tube morphology for subsurface exploration analog work.
analogy_limits: Not a lunar vacuum or radiation analog; Earth basalt chemistry and weathering/biology differ; terrestrial tubes are much smaller.
qualitative_match_assessment: Moderate to high for geology and subsurface morphology; quantitative site matching pending.
next_data_or_validation_step: Candidate region rather than a single surveyed site; select a specific tube/flow and extract Earth DEM, slope, roughness, geology and thermal data.
